doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Simmons drums on Hoosiers
summary: Parker cringes at the loud, dated Simmons drum sound on the film Hoosiers.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Indeed. Did you ever have a circumstance where there’s a whole orchestra recording a film and they had to do it again because of the drummer?

Off hand, yeah. Not any movie that I was on. There’s some that I really — are hard to listen to now. There’s one called “Hoosiers” with Gene Hackman where they wanted me to play Simmons drums. And the producer and the director were really, really keen on the Simmons drum sound, all this electronic stuff. And I see the movie now, even just 30 seconds of it and it makes me cringe because the Simmons drums were so loud in the mix and it sounds so dated, you know it sounds so 70s 80s electronic music. I mean the music itself, the score is good but the drums are way, way too loud in the mix.
